name: CSS Modules
summary: Build-time class-name scoping that keeps you writing ordinary CSS.
what_it_is: A convention where each CSS file is compiled so its class names become locally scoped and unique, imported into a component as an object. The CSS itself is entirely standard.
why_it_matters: CSS Modules solve the single problem that motivated most CSS architecture methodology — global name collisions — without asking you to learn a new way of expressing style. For teams that reject Tailwind on principle but recognise the naming problem is real, this is the most direct answer, and it has aged unusually well.
suitable_for: Teams that want to keep writing standard CSS with scoping handled by the build
Component-based codebases without a utility-class approach
Gradual migration away from global stylesheets
not_suitable_for: Teams wanting a design-token scale supplied for them, rather than authored
verifiable_facts: The official repository documents build-time local scoping of class names.
